question: Why does the cost function matter beyond just measuring error?
direct_answer: Because it determines the learning signal and what kinds of solutions the model prefers.
expanded_answer: The cost function is not just a score; it defines the gradients used for optimization. Different cost functions can make training more sensitive to outliers, favor different tradeoffs, and lead to different inductive biases even with the same architecture.
key_points: Affects inductive bias and solution quality
common_wrong_ideas: Any loss works equally well for any task
The architecture alone determines what the model learns
The cost function only matters at the end of training
